title: Covalent and dative bonding; Lewis structures; Shapes of molecules (VSEPR)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BD03#t4 term and clue written for the game; BD02#t3 term and clue written for the game; BD03#t3 term and clue written for the game; BD02#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BD02#N.2, BD03#N.3a, BD02#N.11, BD03#N.5a, BD02#N.12a, BD03#N.6, BD03#N.9a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Octahedral
items.clue: Shape for six pairs, as in SF₆, with every angle 90°.

items.label: Octet rule
items.clue: The tendency of atoms to end up with eight outer electrons.

items.label: Trigonal bipyramidal
items.clue: Shape for five pairs, as in PCl₅, with angles of 120° and 90°.

items.label: Lone pair
items.clue: Two outer electrons on an atom that are not shared with another atom.

questions.stem: What holds the hydrogen atom and the chlorine atom together in a molecule of hydrogen chloride, HCl?

options.text: The need of each atom to gain a full outer shell by sharing a pair of electrons
The shared pair of electrons itself, acting as a physical link between the atoms
The electrostatic attraction of both nuclei to a shared pair of electrons
The electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions H⁺ and Cl⁻

questions.explanation: The shared pair lies between the H and Cl nuclei and is attracted to both. That attraction is the covalent bond.

questions.stem: Ammonia, NH₃, has three bonding pairs and one lone pair around the nitrogen atom. What is its shape?

options.text: Tetrahedral, as there are four electron pairs around the nitrogen atom
Trigonal planar, as only the three bonding pairs repel one another
Flat, with 90° bond angles, as the atoms are drawn in its dot-and-cross diagram on paper
Pyramidal (trigonal pyramidal), as the lone pair occupies one of four tetrahedral positions

questions.explanation: Four pairs point to the corners of a tetrahedron. Atoms sit at three of them, so N is at the top of a pyramid: about 107°.

questions.stem: Ammonia, NH₃, reacts with a hydrogen ion, H⁺, to form the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺. Which statement about the bonds in NH₄⁺ is correct?

options.text: The bond formed from the lone pair on nitrogen is longer and weaker than the other three N–H bonds
The new bond formed from a pair of electrons supplied by the H⁺ ion to nitrogen
The new bond formed from one electron supplied by nitrogen and one electron supplied by H⁺
All four N–H bonds are identical, although one formed from the lone pair on nitrogen

questions.explanation: The new bond is co-ordinate: both electrons from N. Once formed, all four N–H bonds have the same length and strength.

questions.stem: Predict the H–O–H bond angle in a water molecule, H₂O.

options.text: About 104.5°, as lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs do
About 109.5°, as all four electron pairs around O repel one another equally
About 180°, as the two bonding pairs get as far apart as possible
About 90°, as the H atoms are drawn at right angles in its dot-and-cross diagram

questions.explanation: Two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, arranged tetrahedrally. The lone pairs repel more, squeezing the angle below 109.5°.

questions.stem: Hydrogen cyanide, H–C≡N, has a carbon–nitrogen triple bond. Methylamine, CH₃–NH₂, has a carbon–nitrogen single bond. How does the C≡N bond compare with the C–N bond?

options.text: It is shorter and stronger.
It is longer and stronger.
It is longer and weaker, as six electrons between the nuclei repel each other.
It is the same length and strength, as both bonds join the same two elements.

questions.explanation: Three shared pairs between C and N attract both nuclei more strongly than one pair does, pulling them closer. Shorter and stronger.

questions.stem: Which molecule has four electron pairs arranged tetrahedrally around its central atom, but a non-linear (bent) shape?

options.text: SO₂
CH₄
NH₃
H₂S

questions.explanation: S has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, like O in water: tetrahedral arrangement, and the atoms H–S–H are bent.

questions.stem: In xenon tetrafluoride, XeF₄, the xenon atom (eight outer electrons) forms a single bond to each of four fluorine atoms. What is the shape of XeF₄?

options.text: Tetrahedral, as only its four bonding pairs repel one another around the Xe atom
Octahedral, as there are six electron pairs around the xenon atom
Square planar, as the two lone pairs occupy opposite positions of an octahedron
See-saw, as the two lone pairs occupy adjacent positions, 90° apart, in an octahedron

questions.explanation: 8 − 4 = 4 non-bonding electrons: two lone pairs. They sit 180° apart, leaving four F in a square plane.
